SOURCE SCREENPLAY
=================
Title: Open Frequency
Credit: Written for CineForge UI manual acceptance
Author: CineForge

INT. COMMUNITY RADIO STUDIO - NIGHT

Rain rattles the skylight. Old consoles hum under emergency power.
ARIA threads a tape reel while NOAH coaxes a signal out of a battered mixer.
JUNE covers a whiteboard with road closures, shelter names, and call signs.
KELL rushes in carrying a portable antenna, a dented lantern, and a canvas tool bag.

KELL
Bridge is closed. Cell towers are dead. The hill relay is our only shot.

NOAH
Please tell me that antenna is less cursed than it looks.

KELL
It only tried to kill me once.

JUNE
Good. Tonight we don't have time for a second opinion.

Aria flips a switch. The ON AIR sign flickers, then dies again.

ARIA
Give me ten minutes and one miracle.

JUNE
Take fifteen. Keep the miracle.

CUT TO:

EXT. WATER TOWER CATWALK - NIGHT

Wind lashes the catwalk. The town below is mostly dark except for the high school gym and a gas station canopy.
Aria braces the lantern with her boot while Noah clamps the portable antenna to a rusted rail.
The canvas tool bag swings in the gusts. Somewhere in the valley, a siren rises and cuts out.

NOAH
I miss boring weather.

ARIA
You miss boring jobs.

Noah plugs the cable into a handheld receiver. Static spits, then settles into a thin human voice.

UNKNOWN VOICE (RADIO)
Red Creek station... if anyone hears this... north shelter needs insulin and dry blankets.

Aria and Noah freeze.

ARIA
June, do you copy?

JUNE (RADIO)
Loud enough to make me useful.

Aria smiles for the first time all night and tightens the last bolt.

CUT TO:

INT. HIGH SCHOOL GYM SHELTER - PRE-DAWN

Cots line the basketball court. Handwritten signs point toward MEDICINE, MEALS, and MESSAGES.
June records updates at a folding table while Kell sorts flashlight batteries into a tackle box.
MAYA, a teenager in a soaked marching-band jacket, approaches with a flyer for a missing dog named COMET.

MAYA
Can the station announce this too?

JUNE
If we're naming roads and insulin drops, we can name dogs.

KELL
Comet better be worth interrupting the weather report.

MAYA
He stole my grilled cheese and slept through the evacuation. He's family.

Noah's voice crackles over a tabletop radio.

NOAH (RADIO)
East road is open one lane. Bridge crew wants no heavy trucks till daylight.

June writes the update beneath NORTH SHELTER on the whiteboard, then takes Maya's flyer.

JUNE
Spell his name for the broadcast.

MAYA
C-O-M-E-T. Like the fast kind of star.

CUT TO:

INT. COMMUNITY RADIO STUDIO - MORNING

Wet coats hang from every chair. Pale sunlight cuts through the storm residue on the windows.
Aria pins a hand-drawn map beside the console. Noah labels a notebook DAY TWO.
June tapes a new sign over the door: OPEN FREQUENCY.
Kell enters with a loaf of warm bread wrapped in foil. Maya follows close behind with a muddy, sleepy COMET in her arms.

MAYA
He was under the vending machine in the band room.

KELL
Smart dog. Dry floor, free snacks.

June laughs, reaches for the microphone, and nods at Aria.

JUNE
Red Creek, morning bulletin. East road is open, north shelter is stocked, and one missing dog has been recovered with zero remorse.

Noah pushes up a brass-heavy cassette cue. The room brightens with music.

ARIA
Put that on repeat between updates.

JUNE
No. Once is joy. Twice is branding.

The ON AIR sign steadies into a solid red glow as the four of them settle back to work.
